newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen consolidating on SEC warning.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen consolidating on SEC warning.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to consolidate or fall on Wednesday on a newspaper report that the Securities and Exchange Commission warned local securities investment trust firms not to manipulate stocks, brokers said.

The Economic Daily News said the commission called chief executives from 20 local securities investment trust firms to a meeting late on Tuesday and urged them not to get involved in listed firms' management and not to cooperate with major market players to jointly manipulate stock prices.
On Tuesday, the index ended down 57.07 points at 8,460.63. A 8,350-8,550 range was seen for Wednesday.
Two commission officials reached by Reuters said the commission had held a seminar with local securities trust firms on Tuesday but declined to give details.
The warning was issued after Taiwan's stock market turnover on Tuesday hit an all-time high of T$238.9 billion.
The warning was the second in a row after the SEC on March 20 sent a letter to the island's securities brokerages, urging them to protect investors' rights after recent market rallies.
"Apparently, the SEC does not want to see an overheated market. It wants to cool down the market," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
